doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: Newsletter and writing Dave's autobiography
summary: Iola gave up the newsletter to work on Dave's autobiography and talks about memory.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I want to thank you for your effort you put into the newsletter for those years.

Oh thank you. I sort of hated to give it up but it does take a lot of time and energy and there’s so much else going on and I’m trying to work with Dave to write an autobiography and if I’m going to do that I can’t spend the time with the newsletter. Although I found the newsletter helpful in trying to go back and remember certain events.
Would you have him sit and just talk?
Would you have him sit and just talk about his life?

Yes. And sometimes, you know, the years when I was not traveling with him I’ll ask him a lot of questions and see what he can remember. I think after a while, and it’s true with me too, that everything kind of comes into one. You can’t remember specific events that well. And also it’s true about memory, if it’s a story that you’ve never told it probably won’t come up when you’re trying to think about it. That’s the way the mind works.
Yes. And sometimes we tend to not want to keep the bad parts in the forefront.
Exactly. Push those over to the side.
